_doc: Labeled FAITHFULNESS calibration set for tuning the fact-checker's faithfulness judge (the output->source direction: given SOURCE FACTS + one decomposed CLAIM, is the claim supported?). supported=true when the claim is derivable from the facts by rephrasing / recombination / synonym (a careful reader accepts it) with NO added specific and NO mis-attribution; false when it adds a specific not in the facts, contradicts a fact, mis-attributes a fact to the wrong entity, or overstates scope/certainty. Drawn from REAL author-engine drafts (Conciergerie trajectory 6->3->2) + real Paris facts, so the judge is calibrated on the two measured failure modes: (a) the strict entailer FALSE-NEGATIVES on grounded recombination (blocks convergence), and (b) the author sometimes MIS-ATTRIBUTES a fact (Palais de Justice vs Conciergerie) which must still be caught. For a faithfulness judge the dangerous error is a FALSE POSITIVE (says supported when it is invented -> ships a hallucination); the convergence-killer is a FALSE NEGATIVE (says unsupported when it is grounded recombination).

facts: The westernmost tower facing the Seine is where prisoners were tortured.
Since their screams could be heard across the river, the westernmost tower is called the Tour Bonbec, meaning Big Mouth Tower.
In the 15th century passers-by could still hear the screams of tortured prisoners from the Tour Bonbec.
items.claim: In the fifteenth century, screams of tortured prisoners could be heard from the westernmost tower facing the Seine.
items.note: REAL FN: grounded recombination of the torture + Tour Bonbec + Seine facts; the strict entailer wrongly flagged this
